title: Oh, that noise!
text:
Oh, that noise!. I really want to like this cookware. It's reasonably attractive... for grey hard anodized aluminum cookware. The handles are quite comfortable and also have a hidden hanging ring built into them. The pot walls are decently thick; not so heavy they're hard to use and not so thin then bend and dent easily. The pan bottoms are extra thick so heat distribution is better. The glass lids fit well and the silicone handle allows burn free handling. The whole set is oven safe to 400°. Nothing sticks when cooking and they clean up easily.

With all that being said I hate the noise my utensils make when going across the 'Circulon' bottom of the cookware. It's not that food sticks to it, as I somewhat feared might happen when I first saw the interior of the pans, I've both fried and scrambled eggs in the frying and saute pans without any sticking. It's the 'Zippp..zippp...zippp' noise of every spoon, whisk and spatula going across the ribbed bottom of the pans. It sets my teeth on edge like fingernails on a blackboard.

I'm on the fence about this cookware. It performs well, cleans up easily, except for the handle rivet heads on the inside of the pans which aren't non-stick, goes from stove-top to oven readily but that noise... it really annoys me and makes my cooking experience less enjoyable.

product_metadata.title: Circulon Acclaim Hard Anodized Nonstick 10-Piece Cookware Set
description: This cookware set is an exceptional value, including all of the pans needed to equip your kitchen with the most used cooking pieces. It includes saucepans for whisking a homemade sauce or cooking your morning oatmeal, a big stockpot for soups, stews or boiling pasta, and skillets that will help you turn out perfect crepes or a simple grilled cheese sandwich. The set also includes a saute pan, a wide, straight-sided pan that can perform many of the functions of a skillet but features deep sides for extra capacity - perfect for one dish meals. Start your dish in this pan by sauteing onions and browning meat, then add your liquid and other ingredients into the same pan to finish on the stovetop or in the oven.
